titleFront: This Deal Is Getting Worse All The Time
titleBack: Pray I Don't Alter It Any Further

flipToBack.prose: Flip if Dark Deal on table AND you occupy Bespin system AND you occupy Bespin: Cloud City. All three required.

flipToFront.timing: Required after-trigger; fires on THREE different events: Bespin blown-away last step, Dark Deal just canceled, or isTableChanged with opponent controlling Bespin system.
flipToFront.prose: Flips back if Dark Deal is canceled, OR opponent CONTROLS Bespin system, OR Bespin (system) is 'blown away'. NOTE: losing your own occupation of Bespin/Cloud City does NOT flip it back; only opponent CONTROL of the system does.

children.req: timing trigger: Bespin system blown away
timing trigger: Dark Deal just canceled

requirementSemantics: flipToBack: card-on-table (Dark Deal, canSpot) + OCCUPY x2 (Bespin system, Bespin: Cloud City) - occupy, not control
flipToFront: event triggers (blown-away, cancel) + opponent-CONTROL check; asymmetric with the flip law (your occupation is not re-checked on the back)
back is sticky: you keep the back side even with zero Bespin presence, as long as Dark Deal stays on table, opponent does not control Bespin system, and Bespin is not blown away
typedIdentities: Filters.and(Filters.your(self), Filters.or(Icon.CLOUD_CITY, Icon.JABBAS_PALACE, Icon.SPECIAL_EDITION), Filters.character) vs Filters.Goo_Nee_Tay at Filters.Bespin_location (front immunity)
Filters.and(Filters.Bespin_location, Filters.controlsWith(playerId, self, Filters.Imperial)) (back drain protection)
Filters.All_Too_Easy (back 8-Force loss); Filters.The_Planet_That_Its_Farthest_From targeting Filters.Bespin_system (suspend); Filters.Ugnaught / Filters.alien / Filters.Imperial (back destiny bonus)

profile.runtimeHydration: The generic objective-playbook profile remains disabled. Exact live 109_12 facts are read by TdigwattObjectiveFactsReader from the active physical objective, Dark Deal, Bespin system, and Bespin: Cloud City.
profileGaps: The disabled generic profile does not currently encode the conjunction of one card-on-table leg and two OCCUPY legs; the typed runtime preserves occupation rather than substituting control.
The disabled generic profile does not currently encode the three asymmetric back-side event triggers or the sticky-back rule.
The four-way front upload and back-side alien/Imperial/Ugnaught battle package remain source/card-engine facts outside the disabled generic profile.

missingStateCalculation: TdigwattObjectiveFactsReader binds the active physical objective to canonical front blueprint 109_12, then reads Dark Deal on table plus Dark occupation of Bespin system and Bespin: Cloud City. TdigwattObjectivePolicy.classicFlipReady requires all three and front-side-up.
Occupation is read directly with SpotOverride.INCLUDE_EXCLUDED_FROM_BATTLE. Contested Bespin and Cloud City still satisfy the front law; uncontested control is not substituted.

On the back, TdigwattObjectivePolicy.classicStableBack checks only Dark Deal just canceled, opponent control of Bespin system, and Bespin just blown away. Losing Dark occupation or non-cancellation removal of Dark Deal does not invent a flip-back.
flipPreservation: The exact front objective upload parent receives +200 only with physical-source/action-id provenance and a complete source-legal Reserve candidate. Its exact single-card child receives +400; classic back-side uploads, Vader's Bounty, and cross-print candidates remain neutral or rejected.

Exact engine-offered Dark Deal and classic Cloud City Occupation deploy actions receive +900 only after exact print classification and proof that their source cancellation condition is not already met. Known immediate cancellation is hard-vetoed. When Dark Deal is the final missing front leg, the exact projection also receives the +1200 completion band. The card engine remains the authority for deployment legality.

Classic 109_12 grants no Lando movement action and receives no virtual Lando Force reserve. The persistent-board chain proves the real Dark Deal deploy spends no Force; the printed 3 is destiny, not a deploy cost.

On the back, BattleDecisionPolicy adds only the bounded source payoff after existing formation and predictor safety pass: +2 total battle destiny for the owned alien/Imperial pair, or +4 when one of your Ugnaughts participates.

Existing V21 Force-loss behavior treats Dark Deal as a required classic flip card and selects an ordinary legal loss instead in standalone and combined battle-damage prompts. Off-table Force loss does not alter occupation, so no false TDIGWATT board projection is made.

The pure retention policy proves the exact forfeit margins that would lose a front occupation leg or create opponent system control on the back. No new production caller for the TDIGWATT-specific scoreForfeit method is claimed by this record.
runtimeOwners: TdigwattObjectiveFacts, TdigwattObjectiveFactsReader, and TdigwattObjectivePolicy own exact physical identity, front/back source law, printing-specific pull legality, battle facts, and retention margins.

TdigwattObjectiveScoringPolicy owns bounded semantic contributions and hard-veto boundaries. Mirrored ActionTextEvaluator and CardSelectionEvaluator own the exact parent and child upload decisions; mirrored DeployEvaluator owns exact engine deploy and final-Dark-Deal completion scoring.
BattleDecisionPolicy owns the safety-gated back-side battle payoff. ObjectiveAnalyzer plus mirrored CardSelectionEvaluator retain the existing V21 required-card Force-loss protection.
Rando and Chosen One adapters consume the same shared TDIGWATT facts and policy; parity tests compare their scores, reasons, provenance, and selected action ids.
contradictions: Dark Deal is a mandatory classic flip leg; Cloud City Occupation is an engine card and upload target, not part of the objective's printed flip conjunction.
Occupy is not control. An opponent at either required location does not prevent the classic front flip while Dark still has presence there.
Dark Deal's printed 3 is destiny. The native deploy chain proves the deploy itself does not spend three Force.
Losing occupation after flip is not a flip-back trigger. Dark Deal must be canceled, the opponent must control Bespin system, or Bespin must be blown away.

Pure deploy/retention arithmetic is not itself gameplay proof. This record names the exact production adapters that consume each live rule and leaves unwired forfeit projection as an explicit boundary.

positiveAndNegative: TdigwattObjectiveFactsTest, TdigwattObjectivePolicyTest, TdigwattObjectiveFactsReaderTest, and TdigwattObjectiveScoringPolicyTest lock exact physical identity, all three front legs, contested occupation, sticky-back boundaries, classic pull isolation, deploy bands, safe battle payoff, and loss/forfeit margins.

The same persistent-board test offers the real legal Dark Deal deploy beside Pass after both occupations exist. Both bot paths choose the exact action and destination, retain card provenance, and let the native objective trigger flip.
